implementationPlan.description: TDD the immutable identity/session/capability model. Add table-driven tests for daemon-issued HUMAN/SYSTEM/AGENT principals; profile, session, credential, and exact capability bindings; deterministic sorting/deduplication; defensive copies and deep freezing; rotation preserving principal/profile/scope while revoking the prior generation; stale-generation replay; exact (never wildcard/prefix) project/principal/command/target/transport matching; boundary timestamps; and fail-closed handling of extra keys, throwing getters, proxies/revoked proxies, invalid times, duplicate IDs, and source mutation. Keep this test file <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
`identity-session.test.ts` written, 245 physical lines (cap 250). RED for the right reason: `Cannot find module './identity-capability.js'` — modules absent, not a syntax error.

Read the real contracts surface before asserting against it: `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` is a frozen 90-entry tuple with `isCommandKind`, so `goal.create` and `goal.close` are real kinds and `"goal.*"` / `"not.a.real.command"` are genuinely invalid — the wildcard rejection tests are meaningful rather than tautological.

Model the tests pin. Principal {principalId, kind: HUMAN|SYSTEM|AGENT, profileRevisionId}; Session {sessionId, principalId, profileRevisionId, clientKeyId, transportIds[], status: ACTIVE|CLOSED, expiresAt, generation}; Credential {credentialId, sessionId, generation, revoked}; CapabilityGrant {capabilityId, principalId, projectId, commandKind, targetAggregateId, transportId, requiresRecentStepUp}.

Hostile-input coverage is behavioural, not just shape-based: a throwing getter and a REVOKED PROXY are each asserted twice — once with `.not.toThrow()` and once for a null return — so an unhandled throw cannot be mistaken for a rejection. Defensive copying is proven by mutating the source AFTER snapshotting and by pushing onto the transport array afterwards, which is the aliasing bug a shallow spread would leave open.

Boundary timing is pinned as EXCLUSIVE expiry: usable at 999, NOT usable at 1000 or 1001. That resolves the `now >= expiresAt` ambiguity in one place so step 5 cannot drift, and a CLOSED session is unusable at now=0 regardless.

Rotation asserts increment-exactly-once, previous revoked, current not revoked, and preservation of principal/profile/transports/expiry — plus four refusals: stale generation replayed after a rotation, already-revoked, credential bound to another session, and reuse of the current credential id. Also asserts the credential record contains no key matching bearer/secret/privatekey, so "store no raw secret material" is machine-checked rather than a comment.

Capability matching is proven exact by a five-field table where each field is varied one at a time, plus a dedicated "prefix of a granted target must NOT match" case and an empty-grant-list case. Canonicalization asserts order-independence, exact-duplicate collapse, deep freezing, and rejection of same-capabilityId-different-tuple.

Trimmed from 275 to 245 lines by table-driving two duplicated blocks and compacting fixture literals — no assertion was dropped to fit the cap.

implementationPlan.description: TDD command authentication as a zero-business-effect decision. Through the identity area entrypoint, cover missing/malformed records, bearer/credential swap, principal/profile/session/client-key binding mismatch, absent/false/throwing PoP verification, proof bound to another commandId or requestDigest, closed/revoked/stale-generation and replayed proof, expiry at N-1 versus N, disallowed session transport, absent capability, wrong exact principal/project/command/target/transport, required step-up missing or at expiry, and combined-fault precedence. Assert codes in order AUTHENTICATION_FAILED -> SESSION_REPLAYED -> SESSION_EXPIRED -> CAPABILITY_DENIED, registry-redacted frozen failures with no authorization/effect/event/outbox data, and a deeply frozen success context containing only derived identity/scope facts—never presence, lease, approval, evidence, or TruthClass upgrades. Keep this test file <=250 physical lines and do not treat a valid same-command idempotent retry as credential replay.
implementationPlan.note:
`authenticate-command.test.ts` written, 231 physical lines (cap 250). RED for the right reason: `Cannot find module './index.js'` — exercised through the identity area entrypoint exactly as the plan requires, not by reaching into internals.

Read the real `RuntimeCommandEnvelope` before building fixtures: {commandId, commandKind, correlationId, expectedVersion, payload, requestDigest, schemaVersion, sessionCredential, targetAggregateId} with optional graphRevisionHash/leaseAuthority/policyRevisionHash. It carries an OPAQUE `sessionCredential` and no proof field, which is why the presented proof is a separate injected input rather than something read off the envelope.

Injected-seam design the tests pin: `verifyProof` (crypto over commandId + requestDigest + credentialId + clientKeyId) and `checkReplay` returning "FRESH" | "REPLAYED". Both are injected, and there is an explicit test that a caller-supplied `verified: true` on the proof object grants nothing — the verifier's answer is the only authority.

Precedence pinned as a total order with three combined-fault tests, not just four independent ones: AUTHENTICATION_FAILED beats replay+expiry together; SESSION_REPLAYED beats expiry; SESSION_EXPIRED beats CAPABILITY_DENIED. That ordering matters for a real attack — a forged record that merely looks stale must not be able to select a softer, more specific error than the structural failure it actually is.

Fail-closed on adversarial seams: verifier throws, replay guard throws, replay guard returns "UNKNOWN", and replay guard returns undefined — all AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, and the throwing cases assert `.not.toThrow()` as well as the code, so an escaping exception cannot pass as a rejection. UNKNOWN never authorizes.

Expiry boundary matches the model suite exactly: usable at 999, SESSION_EXPIRED at 1000 and 1001 (`now >= expiresAt`).

The plan's explicit warning is covered: running the same valid command twice is asserted to succeed BOTH times. Credential reuse is not replay — SESSION_REPLAYED is reserved for a proven-stale generation, revoked credential, closed session, or a replay guard that says REPLAYED. Command-level idempotency stays a store concern.

Zero-business-effect is checked positively, not just by absence of a field: on success the context key set must contain none of presence/lease/approval/evidence/truth/effect, and the serialized context must not contain bearer or clientKeyId. On denial, `Object.keys(result)` must be exactly ["ok","error"], `"context" in result` must be false, and the serialized error must contain no outbox/event/effect/authorization/capabilityId.

Fixed a vacuous assertion of my own before completing: I had written `Object.isFrozen(result.context.transportId)`, which is trivially true for a primitive and proves nothing. Replaced with a behavioural check that assigning to `context.principalId` throws TypeError and the value is unchanged.

FOREIGN RED FROM STEP 2 HAS CLEARED — the package now reports 2 failed / 2 passed, where the 2 failures are my own intentional RED and the passes are `project-reducer` and `goal-reducer`. That owner landed their green, so the shared-gate collision I flagged in chat is currently resolved. I will re-verify at step 7 rather than assume it holds.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the minimum daemon-owned identity aggregate and least-authority matcher. In identity-session.ts define closed Principal/ProfileRevision/Session/Credential records, strict hostile-safe snapshot factories, ACTIVE/CLOSED and current-generation semantics, and a pure credential-rotation result that increments exactly once, revokes the old record, preserves bindings/scopes, and never invents renewal policy. In identity-capability.ts define immutable capability grants as exact capabilityId + principalId + projectId + RuntimeCommandKind + targetAggregateId + transportId (+ requiresRecentStepUp), canonicalize them deterministically, reject wildcards/duplicates/unknown shapes, and match only full tuple equality. Store no raw bearer or private-key bytes. Add the one-line strip-types bridges, and keep each production TS file <=250 physical lines with one named responsibility.
implementationPlan.note:
Model suite GREEN: 53/53. `identity-session.ts` (183 lines) and `identity-capability.ts` (146) created with their one-line `.js` strip-types bridges.

identity-session.ts owns the records. `readExact` reads an untrusted value ONCE into a plain own-property map — that single choke point is what contains revoked proxies and hostile getters, since every later check runs against the copy rather than re-invoking a getter. Factories return `null`, never throw. Expiry is exclusive (`now < expiresAt`) matching the pinned boundary tests. `rotateCredential` increments exactly once, revokes the prior record, preserves principal/profile/transports/clientKey/expiry, and deliberately does NOT invent renewal policy — extending expiry is a separate authority. Transports are sorted and deduplicated so two equivalent sessions compare identically. No field on any record can hold bearer or key material; the test asserts that by key name.

identity-capability.ts owns the matcher. Grants are exact 5-tuples plus requiresRecentStepUp; matching is full tuple equality with no wildcard, prefix, or hierarchy path. The `SCOPE_ID` charset deliberately EXCLUDES `*` and `?`, so a grant cannot even carry glob syntax that a future matcher might be tempted to interpret — that is a stronger guarantee than rejecting `"*"` as a special case. A capabilityId reused with a different tuple rejects the whole list rather than picking a winner, so a partially trusted set can never be produced.

A REAL BUG, AND THE THING THAT HID IT. Ten tests failed with `canonicalizeCapabilities` returning null for a perfectly valid grant. Root cause: I imported `isCommandKind` from `@moe/contracts`, but that guard is NOT exported — only the `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` tuple is. The import resolved to `undefined`, calling it threw TypeError, and MY OWN broad `try/catch` swallowed the TypeError into a `null` return, so a genuine import error presented itself as a validation rejection.

Fixed both halves rather than just the symptom:
1. Build the membership Set locally from the exported `RUNTIME_COMMAND_KINDS` — the same "contracts does not export its guards" pattern I hit on @moe/skills. This is now the second package where I have assumed a guard was public and been wrong; the tuple is the public thing, the guard is not.
2. Narrowed the `try/catch` to a `readGrantFields` helper that guards ONLY the property reads. Validation now runs outside it, so a future programming error surfaces as a thrown exception instead of a silent fail-closed null. A broad catch in a fail-closed validator is genuinely dangerous — it converts "my code is broken" into "your input is invalid", which is indistinguishable from correct behaviour in the test output.

`tsc` would also have caught the bad import (TS2305) had I run typecheck before the suite; running the tests first is what let it masquerade. Worth doing typecheck first on any step that adds a cross-package import.

Typecheck currently still reports errors, all in `authenticate-command.test.ts` and all expected at this point: `./index.js` does not exist yet (step 5 creates it) plus some `it.each` tuple-inference noise I will resolve when that entrypoint lands and the file typechecks for real.

implementationPlan.description: Implement authenticateCommand and the identity-only public entrypoint. Consume an already-decoded RuntimeCommandEnvelope plus canonical daemon records, current time, presented proof, an injected cryptographic verifier over an explicit commandId+requestDigest+credential/client-key binding, and an injected authoritative replay guard; never accept caller-supplied `verified: true` as authority. Catch verifier/guard exceptions and unknown outcomes fail closed. Validate structural/cross-record bindings and PoP first (AUTHENTICATION_FAILED), then known closed/revoked/stale generation or replay (SESSION_REPLAYED), then `now >= expiresAt` (SESSION_EXPIRED), then exact session/capability/step-up scope (CAPABILITY_DENIED). Build all failures with @moe/contracts createRuntimeError and return no partial authority; on success return only a copied, deeply frozen authorization context. Export the identity API from identity/index.ts and its one-line bridge only; do not edit packages/core/src/index.ts or implement transport crypto, credential persistence, command idempotency, leases, presence, provider credentials, RBAC, or evidence mutation. Keep each production TS file <=250 physical lines.
implementationPlan.note:
GREEN. `pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck` reports 0 errors; both identity suites pass 95/95 — and they passed on the FIRST run after implementation, which is the payoff for pinning the precedence order and the expiry boundary in tests first.

`authenticate-command.ts` (196 lines) plus `index.ts` (39) and both `.js` bridges. Precedence implemented as a single straight-line sequence so the total order is readable in one pass: bindings and PoP -> replay/generation/closed -> expiry -> transport/capability/step-up.

THE KEY SECURITY PROPERTY, and it is structural rather than a check. The `ProofChallenge` handed to the verifier is REBUILT from the envelope and the daemon-owned records — commandId and requestDigest from the envelope, credentialId from the credential record, clientKeyId from the session record. `input.proof` is validated for binding equality in `bindingsHold` and then never read again. So a caller who attaches `verified: true`, or any other extra field, cannot get it in front of the verifier: there is no code path that reads it. This is stronger than filtering the field, because there is nothing to forget to filter.

`tsc` proved that property rather than me asserting it. TS6133 flagged `const proof = input.proof!` as declared-but-never-read after I finished the function — the unused binding IS the evidence that the proof object is not consulted post-binding. I removed it and left a comment recording why the absence is deliberate, so a future reader does not "helpfully" wire it back in.

Both injected seams are treated as hostile: `verifyProof` and `checkReplay` are each wrapped, any throw becomes AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, `verified !== true` rejects (so a truthy non-boolean does not pass), and any replay outcome outside the exact pair "FRESH"/"REPLAYED" — including undefined and "UNKNOWN" — fails closed. UNKNOWN never authorizes.

Step-up freshness uses a strict `at <= now - STEP_UP_WINDOW` rejection, so the boundary value itself is denied, matching the pinned "at the freshness boundary" test.

Every failure goes through `createRuntimeError({ code, correlationId })`, so the registry supplies retryability, recovery category, next-allowed commands, and truth class. The result object is frozen and contains exactly `{ok, error}` — no partial context escapes on any denial path. On success the context is frozen and carries only derived identity and scope facts.

Ownership respected: `packages/core/src/index.ts` was NOT touched. `identity/index.ts` is the owned public seam; the root re-export belongs to a separate integration task.

Fixed 11 typecheck errors, one real and ten mechanical. The real one was the unused `proof` binding above. The other ten were `it.each` tuple inference — heterogeneous object literals infer a UNION of tuple types that the callback signature cannot absorb — resolved with explicit `as [T, string][]` annotations at 8 sites rather than by loosening any assertion. While repairing one of those tables I dropped a row mid-edit; caught it by re-reading the block and restored the third rotation case, so all three refusal rows are present.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review complete. Typecheck 0 errors, identity suites 95/95. One REAL defect found and fixed.

DEFECT: A stray NUL byte (0x00) was embedded in `identity-capability.ts` line 105 as the `grantKey` join separator — `].join("<NUL>")` instead of a printable delimiter. Found because `grep` reported "Binary file identity-capability.ts matches" during the import-boundary check; `file` classified the source as `data` rather than text.

Impact if shipped: functionally the key still worked (which is why 95/95 tests passed and typecheck was clean — no test could ever catch this), but the file was not valid text. `grep`, `git diff`, and code review tooling all treat it as binary, so this file would have silently dropped out of every future text-based search and review — including the exact security greps in this checklist.

Fixed by a byte-level swap of 0x00 to 0x7c (`|`), which is safe as a delimiter because `SCOPE_ID` excludes it. Verified: 0 raw NUL bytes remain, `file` now reports "JavaScript source, Unicode text, UTF-8 text", and all ten owned files are valid ASCII/UTF-8. Typecheck and tests re-run green after the change.

Three earlier attempts to fix it failed and are worth recording: the Bash tool rejects a command containing a literal control character, and the shell collapsed my `\\u0000` escape back into a raw NUL twice, so string-level replacement kept reinstating the byte. Byte-level Buffer manipulation was the only approach that worked.

Remaining checklist, all clean:
- SIZES, all under the 250 cap: authenticate-command.test 232, authenticate-command 196, identity-capability 145, identity-session.test 248, identity-session 183, index 39. No compression was used to fit; the two tests were table-driven from the start.
- BRIDGES: all four runtime modules have their `.js` strip-types bridge (identity-session, identity-capability, authenticate-command, index). Test files correctly have none.
- IMPORT BOUNDARY: only `@moe/contracts`, relative `./` specifiers, and `vitest` in tests. No reach into `project/**`, `goal/**`, or any other package.
- SECRET LEAKAGE: the single match for bearer/secret/privatekey/password/token across all production sources is a doc comment stating none is stored.
- ACCIDENTAL AUTHORITY: zero occurrences of presence/lease/approval/evidence/truthClass anywhere in production sources — not even in comments.
- NONDETERMINISM: zero hits for Date.now, new Date, Math.random, process.env. `now` is always an injected parameter.
- REPLAY CONFLATION: same-command retry is proven to succeed twice; SESSION_REPLAYED is reserved for proven-stale generation, revoked credential, closed session, or an authoritative REPLAYED verdict.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Rejected implementing a concrete signing/hash algorithm or canonical proof byte format because the authoritative design deliberately does not pin one and transport authentication is out of scope. Rejected a caller-provided boolean proof because it would let adapters grant authority. The plan instead injects a cryptographic verifier bound to commandId/requestDigest/client key plus an authoritative replay guard, while the core owns all binding, freshness, scope, precedence, and fail-closed decisions. Rejected one-time use of the opaque session bearer: credentials are short-lived and reusable; SESSION_REPLAYED applies only to a proven stale/revoked generation or reused proof. Rejected editing the future @moe/core root barrel/scaffold because those paths are outside task ownership.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: @moe/contracts now exports the exact decoded RuntimeCommandEnvelope, RuntimeCommandKind, createRuntimeError, and frozen registry entries for AUTHENTICATION_FAILED, CAPABILITY_DENIED, SESSION_EXPIRED, SESSION_REPLAYED, and IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The command envelope has an opaque sessionCredential but no PoP/signature field, so proof is a separate core input. Same commandId+same request historical replay and commandId+different request IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT remain store/application concerns. The design pins daemon-issued principals, session binding to immutable profile/client/transports/capabilities/OS-local key, zero authority from bearer-only credentials, and no truth/presence upgrade. It does not pin credential TTL, signing algorithm, renewal semantics, wildcard scopes, or error precedence; this plan chooses exact no-wildcard grants and the tested fail-closed order. packages/core is currently absent; the lower-order Project goal lifecycle plan is the coordinated one-time scaffold owner.
